messages:
Chris (support): FYI escalated from @customer-success — DataCo reported SSO failing after a cert rotation. They see 403 on our ACS with 'InvalidSignature' in their IdP logs. Can someone take a look?

Maria (sre): pulling logs for their tenant now. Do we have the raw SAML response from the failed requests? :eyes:

Chris (support): pasted what they provided below: 
```
<samlp:Response ...>
  <saml:Issuer>https://idp.dataco.example</saml:Issuer>
  <saml:Assertion ...>
    <ds:Signature>...</ds:Signature>
    <saml:Subject>...</saml:Subject>
    <saml:Conditions>
      <saml:AudienceRestriction>
        <saml:Audience>https://app.redwoodinference.com/saml/consume</saml:Audience>
      </saml:AudienceRestriction>
    </saml:Conditions>
  </saml:Assertion>
</samlp:Response>
```
They said it worked yesterday and they rotated the IdP signing cert this morning. Error from our side: `SAMLResponse validation failed: Signature verification failed (fingerprint mismatch)`.

Maria (sre): ok that fingerprint bit usually means our stored cert doesn't match the new idp cert. Did they upload new metadata to us or do they rely on the hosted IdP metadata URL?

Chris (support): customer says they updated metadata on their side and that our 'upload metadata' UI shows the old cert until they refresh. They tried re-uploading but still failing. They pasted the metadata XML snippet: 
```
<KeyDescriptor use="signing">
  <KeyInfo>...old cert PEM here...</KeyInfo>
</KeyDescriptor>
<KeyDescriptor use="encryption">
  <KeyInfo>...encryption cert...</KeyInfo>
</KeyDescriptor>
```
They said the IdP admin claims the new cert is active but metadata endpoint returns a document where the signing KeyDescriptor appears after encryption and includes both keys (old and new).

Sanjay (idp-team): could be two things we've seen: 1) our metadata parser picks the first KeyDescriptor with use=signing and ignores the rest (so order matters), or 2) we cache metadata and didn't fetch the updated endpoint. Which path did they use to configure SSO?

Chris (support): they used the hosted IdP metadata URL (auto-fetch) in our tenant settings. UI shows 'last fetched 08:02 UTC' and our DB shows fetch timestamp 1799991000. Customer rotated cert at 08:05 UTC.

Maria (sre): aha — there's your race window. If our fetch ran before rotate, then we still have the old cert. But they said re-uploading metadata didn't help — maybe our upload flow validates and stores the 'first' signing key and we need a manual override. I'll check the fetch logs and parser.

deploy-bot: fetch-metadata job for tenant dataco returned 200 at 1799991200, sha256: abcdef.., parsed 2 KeyDescriptor elements.

Maria (sre): checking parser trace: looks like our SamlMetadataParser takes the first KeyDescriptor where @use=="signing" and sets the signing_cert field. If metadata contains old and new signing keys, but new one comes second, we continue using the old.

Sanjay (idp-team): that's a bug — IdPs rotate keys by publishing both keys in metadata to allow in-flight assertions to be verified. Parser should prefer latest certificate based on <ds:X509Certificate> validity period (NotBefore/NotAfter) or at least prefer the key whose thumbprint matches the Assertion Signature. But we don't currently inspect NotBefore.

Maria (sre): reproduction steps for dev: 
1) create metadata with two KeyDescriptor entries for signing: old (expired soon) then new;
2) configure tenant to use metadata URL;
3) rotate cert and post combined metadata;
4) simulate SAML response signed with new cert -> verify we reject.

Chris (support): customer asked for a workaround while we fix it. They can either: a) re-order elements in the published metadata so signing key appears first (not ideal), or b) upload the new cert manually in the tenant settings (there's an upload cert field). They said upload didn't take previously — do we have a bug there?

Maria (sre): I looked at the upload flow logs: upload API accepted the file but our metadata normalizer strips duplicate KeyDescriptors and canonicalizes order, preserving the first encountered signing key. So manual upload that still contains both keys will keep the old. If they upload just the new cert (single signing KeyDescriptor) it should pick up.

Sanjay (idp-team): longer term: we'll change parser to evaluate X509Data validity period and prefer certs whose NotBefore<=now<=NotAfter, or to compare fingerprint against the signature in the SAMLResponse (if provided) to auto-select correct key. Filing a ticket.

Maria (sre): created internal ticket INF-2487: "SAML metadata parser should prefer active signing certs when multiple KeyDescriptors present". Assigning to @sanjay. Est: small patch + tests, hotfix to prod asap.

Chris (support): customer wants immediate steps. Suggested steps I offered: 
- Ask IdP admin to publish metadata with only the new signing KeyDescriptor (temporary) OR
- Export the new signing cert from IdP and use our 'Upload Signing Certificate' in tenant settings (upload only the new cert), OR
- If they use hosted metadata URL, wait ~5-10m for our refetch job then toggle SSO off/on in UI to force re-validate.

Customer reply (via support): "We uploaded only the new signing cert and the login is working again. We also want a permanent fix so our usual rotation procedure doesn't fail" :thumbsup:

Maria (sre): noted. I'll push a small change to parser to prefer certificates whose subject/validity looks current and add a migration script to re-evaluate tenants with multiple signing keys. Will post PR link once ready.

Sanjay (idp-team): PR: https://git.internal/redwood/saml-parser/pulls/123 — implements NotBefore/NotAfter check and preferential selection. Includes unit tests for ordering and mixed-key metadata.

Maria (sre): rolling out hotfix to staging now, will run through canary on prod auth cluster after confirmation from QA.

deploy-bot: deploy to staging started (job 4523) at 1799993000.

Chris (support): customer confirmed workaround works. I'll close the escalation once patch is in prod. Saved their failing SAMLResponse so we can add an integration test that signs with the new cert.

Maria (sre): follow-ups: add clearer instructions in KB about cert rotation best practices (publish new key first AND ensure metadata endpoint returns only the new signing KeyDescriptor if possible), and add a console warning when multiple signing keys are present.

Chris (support): thanks team. Leaving thread open until prod rollout. :white_check_mark:
